messages:
maria: FYI spotted something odd during the policy rollout smoke tests — analytics-role unexpectedly succeeded in writing to s3://redwood-analytics-raw. Not normal for that role. :eyes:

maria: Audit event (from our central logger):
```json
{
  \"eventTime\": \"2026-03-20T14:02:31Z\",\n  \"eventName\": \"PutObject\",\n  \"userIdentity\": { \"type\": \"AssumedRole\", \"arn\": \"arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/analytics-role/session-123\" },\n  \"requestParameters\": { \"bucketName\": \"redwood-analytics-raw\", \"key\": \"ingest/2026-03-20/abc.json\" }\n}
```

maria: The timing matches the new role mapping merge that went out ~13:58 UTC.

jon: Ugh. Can we confirm this is not a duplicate role with broader perms? Do we have the diff from the rollout PR? @anya can you paste the IAM policy diff?

anya: pasting the minimal diff I applied in the refactor PR:
```hcl
- policy \"analytics-readonly\" {\n-  statement { actions = [\"s3:GetObject\"] resources = [\"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-analytics-raw/*\"] }\n-}\n+ policy \"analytics\" {\n+  statement { actions = [\"s3:GetObject\", \"s3:PutObject\"] resources = [\"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-analytics-raw/*\"] }\n+}\n```

anya: I thought PutObject was gated by a separate ingest-service role; looks like my rename collapsed the two policies. Sorry, totally my mistake. :grimacing:

sam (sec): Ok — we need an immediate containment plan. Steps: 1) Add explicit Deny for s3:PutObject to analytics-role (org-level override) 2) Revoke any active STS sessions for that role 3) Run quick S3 object audit/manifest for last 24h 4) Check KMS key policy for any grants tied to analytics-role.

maria: I'll take 1+2 now. Applying an org-level deny via `aws iam put-role-policy` (quick snippet):
```bash
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name analytics-role --policy-name deny-s3-put-temp --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-analytics-raw/*","Condition":{}}]}'
```

leo: For 2) to force STS session invalidation, rotate the role's trust or remove inline session tags? We usually revoke by rotating the role credentials for long-lived keys — but for assumed roles, we can update the trust and that will prevent new assumes; existing session tokens still valid until expiration. Consider using an STS session revocation approach: block at bucket policy level is faster.

sam (sec): Good call. Also check the KMS key: if PutObject used server-side encryption with customer-managed key, analytics-role might have been granted kms:GenerateDataKey via the key policy. If so, revoke that grant and rotate key if necessary.

anya: Looking at the KMS key policy for arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-1234, there is a statement that grants Encrypt and GenerateDataKey to a role group that included analytics-role after the refactor. I will remove that principal now.

maria: Done with the temporary deny and opened a ticket with infra to do a forced bucket policy block as well. CLI returned success at 14:05:12 UTC.

deploy-bot: policy-change deployed -- id: pc-8421 -- targets: analytics-role -- env: prod -- ts: 1951234588

jon: Good. Next: forensic sweep. Maria/Anya, please run `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-analytics-raw --query 'Contents[?LastModified>=\`2026-03-19T14:00:00Z\`]'` and capture MD5s/tags. We need a list of objects created/modified by that role.

maria: Running that now, will attach results to INCIDENT-2026-03-20-04.

leo: I'll start a quick check in Athena against access_logs to find PutObject entries and list distinct principals. If we see other principals, escalate.

sam (sec): Communication: do not message customers. This is internal. Tag incident_sev2. Also re-evaluate CI/CD gating to prevent merging policy renames without an RBAC-owner signoff.

anya: I'm drafting a PR to split the policies again and add an automated linter to flag combined statements that expand write perms. Will include a test that verifies 'analytics' role lacks s3:PutObject.

maria: Quick mitigation checklist completed: deny applied, KMS principal removed, ticket created, object list in progress. Will update in 30m.

jon: Thanks everyone. After we validate no unauthorized writes, we'll rollback the refactor commit and reapply a corrected change in canary + review.

maria: Update 14:16 UTC — Athena shows 4 PutObject events by analytics-role between 13:59 and 14:03. Objects are small ingestion files, no PII detected in previews. Continuing content review.

sam (sec): Good triage. After containment and verification, schedule a postmortem focused on process gap (policy rename testing). Assigning action owners: anya -> policy linter, leo -> access log alerting rule, jon -> revise rollout checklist, maria -> forensic report.

maria: I'll attach the forensic dump to the ticket once done. Closing interim actions, will reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
